title: LE review criteria

source.name: EllyDTrades LE Model: Strategy Research & Bot Spec
source.note: Checklist derived for this journal. Grade A was stated plainly. Grade B was stated in contradictory ways. Grade D was not published. B and D items have no numeric threshold and stay 'needs your confirmation'. This app does not trade and does not connect to a broker.

grades.A: Stated plainly by him or the official indicator docs
grades.B: Stated, but sources contradict each other
grades.D: Not published. No number is stored for this item.

personal_rules_policy: His account-guide examples are reference only. Do not copy them into personal rules. Daily trade limits and daily loss limits stay blank until you set them.
gate_order: Level gate: 10-minute candle body beyond both levels
EMA gate: correct side of the 10-minute 8 EMA

items.label: PDH and PDL
items.statement: PDH and PDL are the prior regular-session high and low. Prior-day levels outweigh pre-market levels.

items.label: PMH and PML
items.statement: PMH and PML are the pre-market high and low from 4:00 to 9:29 ET. Thin pre-market wicks are not real extremes; use where price is basing. No volume cutoff is published.

items.label: Body beyond both levels
items.statement: For a long, the 10-minute candle body must clear both PMH and PDH. For a short, both PML and PDL. A wick through a level is not a break.

items.label: Levels before the EMA
items.statement: A level has to break before an 8 EMA entry is allowed. Do not buy the EMA if no level has broken.

items.label: 10-minute 8 EMA
items.statement: The traded moving average is the 8 EMA on the 10-minute chart, with smoothing off. Price should be above it for longs and below it for shorts.

items.label: 8 EMA near the level
items.statement: On a level retest, the 8 EMA should be near the level being retested. How near is the unpublished air-gap item, not a number in this file.

items.label: Air-gap tolerance
items.statement: The buffer that decides a level retest versus an EMA entry is not published. It lives in the paid indicator. Nothing here fills that in.

items.label: Level retest
items.statement: After the body clears a level, a level entry is a pullback that retests the level and holds.

items.label: 8 EMA entry
items.statement: An EMA entry marks the first candle that touches the 8 EMA, then enters when price breaks that candle's high (long) or low (short).

items.label: Whichever entry comes first
items.statement: Take the level retest or the EMA entry, whichever arrives first.

items.label: VIX filter
items.statement: VIX above 20 blocks longs. This is a market filter, checked before the level gate. If VIX was not imported, the item is insufficient data.

items.label: First 30 to 60 minutes
items.statement: A level break that happens inside the first 30 to 60 minutes of the regular session and holds is the high-conviction version. Failing PMH in the first 30 minutes is chop or a gap fill. The journal records which window the fill was in. It does not invent a single minute cutoff.

items.label: Gap-down play
items.statement: On a gap down, if QQQ or SPY is still holding PML at 10:00 ET, the play is a long for a pop. If PML breaks, there is no trade.

items.label: Gap-down target
items.statement: Two examples exist and the formula was never written. Do not compute a target percent. Leave the target for you to confirm.

items.label: 30-minute chart
items.statement: The 10-minute chart is the entry timeframe. The 30-minute chart is context and the exit timeframe. The 3-minute chart is for the open only.

items.label: 30-minute extension limit
items.statement: A numeric extension limit, if one exists, was not published. The 30-minute role above is the timeframe, not a distance.

items.label: Volume and momentum threshold
items.statement: Relative volume is a scanner column. No cutoff number was published. Do not treat a bar as confirmed or fake from a guessed multiple.

items.label: Stop at the entry-candle extreme
items.statement: For options, the stop is the low of the entry candle for a long and the high for a short, acted on immediately, with no wait for a candle close. If no stop was imported, say so. Do not invent the price.

items.label: Which candle is the entry candle
items.statement: It is unresolved whether the stop candle is the touch candle or the break candle. The journal does not pick one.

items.label: Scale at the high or low of day
items.statement: Take part off at the high of day for longs or the low of day for shorts, then trail the rest with the 8 EMA and cut when price breaks it. The fraction is the separate unconfirmed item.

items.label: Scaling fraction
items.statement: Sources have said half, one third, two of three, and 75 percent. No single fraction is enforced.

items.label: Trail the runner with the 8 EMA
items.statement: After the first scale-out, move the stop to the 8 EMA and trail it. Cut the remainder when price breaks the 8 EMA.

items.label: Reduce risk at 10:00 ET
items.statement: Reduce risk at 10:00 ET. Flat before the close on same-day expiry.

items.label: 1 to 2 strikes out of the money
items.statement: The published strike guide is 1 to 2 strikes out of the money. The journal can compare a computed strike distance with that range. It does not invent a different distance.

items.label: No trade between PML and PMH
items.statement: No trade while price is between PML and PMH.

items.label: Outside setup
items.statement: Being beyond both levels is the stronger, A+ version of the setup.

items.label: Inside day
items.statement: The indicator still marks an inside setup. Later video says to avoid inside days. Leave this for you to confirm. Do not auto-fail it.

items.label: Daily chart agrees
items.statement: The daily chart overrides the intraday chart. A bearish daily means no longs. The mechanical version he described uses the daily 8 EMA and daily 20 EMA.

items.label: Index products use PDH and PDL only
items.statement: For index products, use PDH and PDL only.

items.label: Adds
items.statement: Adds named in his recaps: clearing the second level, reclaiming the 8 EMA, or a flag. He has described entering on a PMH retest and adding over PDH.

items.label: His size and loss examples
items.statement: On a small-account guide he used about 20% of the account as a max position, about 6% as a max daily loss, and a three-trade cap with two reds ending the day. Those are his examples. They are not your settings and the journal will not prefill them.
